These are lexical static-analysis metrics, calculated from physical source lines. Cyclomatic complexity starts each procedure at 1 and adds decisions for IF, ELSE IF, DO, SELECT CASE, CASE, WHERE, and FORALL. Cognitive complexity uses the same decisions with a nesting penalty. Argument counts are parsed from the procedure header, including continuation lines. Because it is not a full Fortran parser, use the complexity values for comparative analysis; compiler-aware tooling is required for audit-grade results.

Definitions: fan-out counts distinct names a procedure calls (CALL statements plus references matching a function defined in this source tree); fan-in counts distinct procedures calling a name, shared by same-named definitions (see the Defs column). Module coupling: Ca = units that USE the module, Ce = distinct modules USEd anywhere in it, instability I = Ce/(Ca+Ce). Internal-call ratio = resolved calls staying in the file; shared-dependency ratio = procedure pairs in the file sharing a USE module or COMMON block. Resolution is by name, not scope: an array reference shadowing a function name counts as a call, and generic or same-named procedures are merged. Use these for comparative analysis, not compiler-grade dependency extraction.

Definitions: a call edge is a distinct (caller, callee) name pair from CALL statements plus references matching a function defined in this source tree. An edge is explicit-interface when the callee is a module procedure and the caller USEs that module, is that module, or is defined in it; other edges to corpus-defined procedures are implicit-interface, and edges to undefined names (intrinsics or true externals) are unresolved and excluded from the coverage percentage. Resolution is by name, not scope: an array reference shadowing a function name counts as a call, same-named procedures merge, and USE-visibility ignores ONLY lists and renames. Use this as a progress trend, not compiler-grade interface checking.

Analysis is name-based on the pre-semantic parse tree. COMMON consistency compares each unit's member-name sequence (multiple COMMON statements for one block in a unit concatenate); it cannot see storage association through EQUIVALENCE, type/kind differences between same-named members, or deliberate sequence-association aliasing, and a name-only mismatch may be intentional renaming. Module variables count entities declared in a module's specification part, excluding PARAMETER constants; variables of CONTAINS'd procedures are locals and excluded. SAVE attributes on type declarations are not counted as SAVE statements. The headline total counts distinct (block, member) pairs plus module variables; the same name in two blocks is two variables.

Classification is per dummy argument: assumed-size means the declared last dimension is *, adjustable means an explicit-shape bound references a name that is not a PARAMETER constant declared in the same file (so bounds using USE'd module constants are counted as adjustable), and assumed-length character covers CHARACTER*(*) and CHARACTER(LEN=*). Assumed-shape (:) and deferred-shape dummies are the modern target and are not flagged. ENTRY-point argument lists are not analyzed.

9. Mixed-Precision Risk Census

Line-scanner counts on logical statements: comments and character literals are stripped before matching and continuation lines are joined, so a WRITE inside a quoted string or a unit split across a continuation is handled. Logical-IF prefixes (IF (...) WRITE(...)) are stripped before classification. The unit is the first control-list item (after an optional UNIT=): an integer literal counts as hardcoded, * as console, any other name or expression as variable; internal-file WRITEs to a character variable are indistinguishable from variable units here. Statement counts cover READ/WRITE/OPEN/CLOSE/REWIND/BACKSPACE/ENDFILE/INQUIRE and PRINT.
